title: Degree-zero cohomology of the constant coefficients on a connected scheme
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $Y$ be a nonempty connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] separated finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $k$-scheme, and use the cohomology groups $H^0(Y,\Lambda)=H^0(Y,\Lambda_Y)$ of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] for $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E\}$, with $(A_{E,n})_Y$ the constant sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients].

1. For every $n\geq1$, let $1_n\in H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$ be the unit class and let $u_n:A_{E,n}\to H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$ be the constant-section map induced by the resolution augmentation and exact point sections; $u_n$ is bijective and $u_n(1)=1_n$.

2. Define the coefficient-reduction maps $Q_n:H^0(Y,A_{E,n+1})\to H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$ and the projection-induced maps $P_n:H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)\to H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$ from the specified `sfDirectImageTransition`, `SfIntegralDirectImage.projection`, the finite-reduction comparison, and the identity-on-sections coefficient-restriction comparison [def-trf-point-reduction-units]. They satisfy $Q_n\circ P_{n+1}=P_n$. The compatible tuples form $\varprojlim_n H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$. There is an isomorphism $H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_nH^0(Y,A_{E,n})$, with $P_n(1_{\mathcal O_E})=1_n$, and $a\mapsto a\cdot1_{\mathcal O_E}$ is bijective.

3. The recorded rational tensor comparison identifies $H^0(Y,E)$ with $H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ and sends $1_{\mathcal O_E}\otimes1$ to $1_E$. The map $E\to H^0(Y,E)$, $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\cdot1_E$, is bijective.

proof.text: Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $F_n=(A_{E,n})_Y$. The module-sheaf categories on the chosen small pro-etale sites are Grothendieck by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], hence have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Choose $F_n\to I_n^\bullet$ with $I_n^j=0$ for $j<0$ using [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero](1). This bounded-below injective complex is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so [def-weil-derived-direct-image] computes $Ra_{Y*,n}F_n$ by $a_{Y*}I_n^\bullet$. Direct image is left exact by [lem-weil-proetale-module-direct-image-left-exact], and part (2) of the degree-zero lemma gives $\mathcal H^0(Ra_{Y*,n}F_n)=a_{Y*}F_n$. Exact point sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] identify $H^0(\Gamma(s,a_{Y*}I_n^\bullet))$ with $\Gamma(s,a_{Y*}F_n)=F_n(Y)$; the last equality is the evaluation formula in [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image], since $s\times_sY=Y$. By [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] this is $H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$. All complexes used have zero terms in negative degrees, so $H^{-1}(Y,A_{E,n})=0$ as well. The identifications are induced by the resolution augmentation and evaluation, hence send constant sections to their degree-zero classes.

proof.text: Give the additive group $T=A_{E,n}$ the discrete topology. Addition and negation are continuous because every map between discrete spaces is continuous. The existing Mathlib leaf [lem-cbc-continuous-functions-fpqc-sheaf] says that $L_T(U)=C(|U|,T)$, with pointwise addition and restrictions by precomposition, is an fpqc sheaf on schemes. Every pro-etale covering is fpqc by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], so restriction to $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is a sheaf. A map to a discrete space is continuous exactly when it is constant on some open neighbourhood of every point: inverse images of singletons are open, and conversely the inverse image of any subset is the union of those open fibres. Pointwise multiplication and the constant function $1$ make $L_T$ a sheaf of rings as well: these operations preserve continuity into the discrete ring, and all ring identities are pointwise equalities.

The map from the constant presheaf $P_T(U)=T$ to $L_T$ sends $t$ to the constant function with value $t$. It exhibits $L_T$ as the sheafification in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]: for any presheaf map $P_T\to G$ with $G$ a sheaf, and any $f\in L_T(U)$, cover $U$ by the open fibres $f^{-1}(t)$ and glue the images in $G$ of their constant values $t$. These are pro-etale coverings by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; intersections with different values are empty and an abelian sheaf has only its zero section on the empty object. On overlaps with the same value the images agree by naturality. Intersecting two such open covers proves independence, and pulling back the cover proves compatibility with restrictions; intersecting the covers for two functions proves additivity. Every extension must have these local values, so uniqueness follows from the sheaf condition. For a map $P_T\to G$ of ring-valued presheaves into a sheaf of rings, the same extension preserves multiplication by intersecting the constant-value covers of two functions, and preserves $1$ on every member of the cover. Thus the ring version of [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] identifies $(A_{E,n})_Y$ with $L_T$, carrying each constant section to its constant function. This construction commutes with a coefficient homomorphism $T\to T'$: on every open where $f=t$ both composites give the image of $t$, and uniqueness of gluing gives equality globally.

proof.text: Choose $y\in Y$, possible by the nonemptiness in [def-weil-connected-scheme]. For $f\in L_T(Y)$ the fibre $f^{-1}(f(y))$ is nonempty and clopen, since both it and its complement are inverse images of open subsets of the discrete space $T$. Connectedness makes its complement empty. Therefore $f$ is the constant function $f(y)$. Conversely distinct constants give distinct functions by evaluation at $y$. Together with Steps 1 and 3 this proves that $A_{E,n}\to H^0(Y,A_{E,n})$ is an isomorphism of additive groups, equal to $a\mapsto a\cdot1$. It is $A_{E,n}$-linear: multiplication by $a$ sends the constant section $b$ to the constant section $ab$, which can be checked before sheafification and then on the same open covers. The coefficient-naturality at the end of Step 3 shows that the reduction maps send the section $a$ to the section $a\bmod\varpi_E^n$; hence these isomorphisms identify the entire inverse system with $(A_{E,n})_n$.

proof.text: Let $B_n=\operatorname{Res}_n Ra_{Y*,n}F_n$ and $B=Ra_{Y*}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$. By [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible](2), and [def-weil-derived-direct-image], $B=R\varprojlim_nB_n$ with its canonical projections. Applying [lem-kun-site-rgamma-derived-limit] on $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and using exact point sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] gives $\Gamma(s,B)\simeq R\varprojlim_n\Gamma(s,B_n)$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$, with the original projection maps. Use the small skeleton fixed in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the ring sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$ and final object $s$; reindex $n=m+1$ for the lemma's $m\geq0$ convention.

proof.text: Restriction of scalars does not change underlying sections. By [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], $\Gamma(s,B_n)$ computes $H^i(Y,A_{E,n})$ and $\Gamma(s,B)$ computes integral cohomology. The map $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n+1}\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ of the tower corresponds to the reduction $F_{n+1}\to F_n$ under the canonical isomorphisms of [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible](2), since both of these isomorphisms are induced by the projections and $\pi_n$ is the reduction composed with $\pi_{n+1}$. Apply [lem-pod-constant-tower-transition] with $f=a_Y$, $A=A_{E,n+1}$, $B=A_{E,n}$ and $u:F_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}F_n$ the reduction. The transition in [def-weil-derived-direct-image] is exactly the composite in that node. Exact point sections [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] therefore identify its $H^0$ map with $F_{n+1}(Y)\to F_n(Y)$. By Step 4, this is coefficient reduction $A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n}$.

proof.text: Step 1 gives $H^{-1}(\Gamma(s,B_n))=0$, which is finite. Therefore the degree-zero case of [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler] applies to the tower in Step 5 and identifies the canonical projection map $H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)\to\varprojlim_nH^0(Y,A_{E,n})$ as an isomorphism. No finiteness of higher cohomology is needed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules](2) to $M=\mathcal O_E$, generated by $1$ as an $\mathcal O_E$-module. It gives the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_n\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E=\varprojlim_n A_{E,n}$; the quotient rings and transition maps are exactly those of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. By the inverse-system compatibility of Step 4 and the projection comparison of Step 7, this proves clause (2). Its distinguished element $1_{\mathcal O_E}$ maps to the system $(1\bmod\varpi_E^n)_n$, so the inverse isomorphism $\mathcal O_E\to H^0(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ is $a\mapsto a\cdot1_{\mathcal O_E}$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], the rational coefficient object is represented by the integral coefficient object and $Ra_{Y*}$ at $E$ is its rationalization, as stipulated in [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. By [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point](3), its cohomology complex is $C^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$, where $C^\bullet=\Gamma(s,Ra_{Y*}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})$. In [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], every nonzero element of $E$ is $u\varpi_E^m$ for a unit $u\in\mathcal O_E$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, so $E=\mathcal O_E[1/\varpi_E]$. Its inclusion satisfies the localization conditions (every element is a fraction, powers of $\varpi_E$ are invertible, and the kernel is zero), hence [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat] gives flatness. Flat tensor product preserves the kernel of $d^0$ and the image of $d^{-1}$, and preserves the quotient of the former by the latter. Therefore $H^0(C^\bullet\otimes E)=H^0(C^\bullet)\otimes E$, which is the equality in clause (3) by [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Tensor the unit isomorphism of Step 8 with $E$: its inverse tensors to an inverse, and $1_{\mathcal O_E}\otimes1=1_E$, so the resulting isomorphism is precisely $\lambda\mapsto\lambda\cdot1_E$.
